cells.tense: Your strength is out where it can do work, and it's holding steady.
cells.ask: Before you carry one thing this week, say what you want back from it. Let the answer, or the quiet, be the end.
cells.core:
What you have to offer is out where it can do work, and it's holding. Strength goes into things by measure, not in a flood — some of what comes at you is yours to carry and the rest isn't, and that line is still drawn by you. The work you've been building has mostly finished taking its shape. It hasn't been called complete yet.

What feeds this next isn't more effort on the same thing. It's aim. One direction, picked on purpose, so what you put out has somewhere to land instead of spreading thin wherever there's a pull. Say that direction plainly, where it will be heard. Strength keeps moving and one clear aim decides where it goes — that's the whole of what's left here.
cells.sheetLine: Your strength is out doing work, held to a measure you still keep.
cells.verb: putting your strength out where it can do work
cells.place: where what's been built reaches the point of being handed on

cells.tense: You're braced for a shortfall that hasn't been announced yet.
cells.ask: Give to one person this week, then leave. No follow-up, no patching the gap you spot on your way out.
cells.core:
You've been handing out ahead of what's needed. The shortfall hasn't arrived and you're already there with your hands out. You tally as you go — who gave less, who owes more, what to put in to bring it level — and that arithmetic costs more than the putting in does.

Carrying a lot doesn't require bracing under it. There's a way to hold a great weight and let it stay contained instead of crushed, and it opens when you trust the exchange rather than audit it. Put something in this week and leave it there. Let the person take it without you standing over the trade. Move like a person, not a bookkeeper, and the bracing has nothing left to brace against.

cells.tense: You closed a door on this and you've been standing at it since.
cells.ask: One finished piece of work you didn't call finished — stand it up and say out loud that it's done. Then pick up what comes after.
cells.core:
There's strength you stopped putting out. Something you were carrying got set down, and the outward move — strength going where it can do work, by measure — hasn't restarted. What you have to offer is still intact. It's sitting still.

What's behind you is a finish that didn't get marked. You're at a door that already closed, and nothing new opens while the last thing stays unclaimed. What you're out of reach of is holding that contains without forcing. You don't get back to it by making yourself care again.

Take one small thing and finish it on purpose, all the way to the end, and let it be over. The release that comes with it is the way back in — not a loss, just what completion feels like when you let it land.
cells.sheetLine: What you give stopped somewhere behind you, and it's still waiting there.

cells.tense: Your strength keeps moving out toward people and you file it as nothing.
cells.ask: Name one thing you do that only works because you're there. Say it to the person it helps, once, and let it stand.
cells.core:
Strength keeps moving out of you toward people who can use it, and it works. You call it nothing, call it what anyone would do, so it flows without being yours. What you put out goes unclaimed by the only person it belongs to.

The way back runs through something simpler than strategy. There's a light you'd steer by, an aim you'd choose if you said it aloud — and you've been shining from a place you grew on purpose without admitting you grew it. So name it. One thing you're the source of, said plainly to one person, today. Not a boast — a claim. When the aim comes back under your own name, what you put out stops being automatic and starts being yours.
cells.sheetLine: Your strength is already flowing out. You just haven't signed it.

attempts.check: The draft kept implying that the person has people depending on them and that resources are actually moving, which the record only says of the card's line outward and never of the person's situation — a reader with nobody relying on them or with plenty on hand could rightly say this isn't happening. The asks don't lean on that picture, so they hold even if the read is wrong: each is one act inside the person's own work that teaches them the movement either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line where the care they give is already load-bearing for others — it's the flattering version of the card and I cut it.
